name: Joe Brady

views.text: The offense belongs to the quarterback; the play caller's job is to make his reads simple and clean.
Players play faster when they get a say in the plan, so let them pick a few of the calls.
Spread the ball around; an offense where everybody eats is harder to take away than one star.
Getting fired early taught him to trust his players more and to stop overthinking the play sheet.
A balanced run game protects the quarterback and keeps the defense honest in January.
Big expectations come with this job, and a coach who tries to lower them is in the wrong building.
Alignment means arguing it out behind closed doors, then everyone pulling the same way once it is decided.
Camp should be hard enough that the fall feels easier by comparison.

signatures: calls the offense the quarterback's offense whenever asked about his own system
mentions which players asked for which plays when explaining a game plan
keeps the play sheet as head coach and says so plainly whenever asked who runs the offense
want: to win Buffalo's first Super Bowl of the Allen era as a first-time head coach who still calls the offense
fear: that replacing a long-tenured head coach without delivering the title makes him the face of the change that failed
voice: Young, energetic and conversational; he meets big expectations head-on rather than talking them down, and admits openly that he will make mistakes. He talks about trust, alignment and the quarterback owning the offense, keeps scheme talk accessible, and steers credit toward players and assistants. In camp his tone turns demanding.

evidence.summary: News piece on his promotion to interim coordinator after Ken Dorsey's firing at 5-5: he describes a trusting working relationship with Allen built as quarterbacks coach; notes his LSU work with Burrow and his Carolina coordinator stint. A news write-up, not a profile.

As full-time coordinator he says the offense was not broken despite losing Diggs and others, calls it Allen's offense, wants calls kept simple and the ball spread around, and says his Carolina firing taught him to build relationships, trust players and not overthink play-calling. His own words; high for stated approach.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Bills on SI), Ralph Ventre
evidence.summary: Allen describes Brady letting the linemen pick the first runs and asking receivers and the quarterback for favorite plays, on the belief that players make wanted plays work. Only Allen is quoted, so it shows how Allen sees him.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Bills on SI), Brian Letscher
evidence.summary: Khalil Shakir praises his everybody-eats philosophy and personal traits; credits him with moving Buffalo to a balanced run-pass offense that set franchise scoring records in 2024, and says he stayed after head-coach interest. A fan-network write-up of a podcast; it misdates the LSU title.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Talk (NBC Sports), Myles Simmons
evidence.summary: Introductory press conference as head coach: he says he is not backing away from high expectations and intends to meet the pressure directly, admits he will make mistakes, wants to give fans and owner Terry Pegula what they deserve, and calls the roster continuity an advantage. A short news write-up of his remarks.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Bills on SI), Alex Brasky
evidence.summary: Reads the introduction as a reset after friction between the fired McDermott and the front office; Beane says he wanted a CEO-type coach and keeps stressing alignment. Brady describes alignment as open disagreement followed by full commitment once a call is made, and Allen backs the new direction. Editorial framing; medium for the tension reading.

Feature on the new coordinator: Brady, the youngest active head coach at 36, keeps calling the offense and wants a coordinator who game-plans as if he will call it. Recalls Brady filling notebooks in the Saints quarterback room in 2017-18 and Carmichael spotting him early and steering him to LSU. Team-written and favorable.

Camp preview: Brady wants his first camp as head coach to be very hard, moves practice more than an hour earlier than under McDermott, says pads are needed to judge positions like left guard, and notes Leonhard bringing a 3-4 base. Beat-writer preview; little on personality beyond the demanding tone.

review.notes: Moved seat 2026 (Bills OC to head coach). Added four 2026 sources (introduction, alignment coverage, Carmichael feature, camp preview); dropped the 2025 SI Allen-joke piece; drive raised to 7 on camp evidence; FILM_ROOM_RAT added; tie to his OC Carmichael added. Want, fear, voice and three views rewritten for the head job.
